name: Galice Creek Athapaskan
confidence_why: The only statement on Galice stress is Landar's 1977 remark that, as Hoijer had observed, stress and pitch are not phonemic in Oregon Athabaskan, but Hoijer's own 1966 sketch says nothing about stress, Hoijer 1960 speaks only of the absence of tone, and Krauss 1979 calls Pacific Coast Athabaskan stress an unresolved problem, so neither a placement nor a system can be stated for Galice.

catalog_quote: (6) Stress: I show three degrees of loudness, primary (acute at onset of chest pulse), secondary (grave at onset), and weak (not marked). (7) Pitch: I show high pitch by acute accent; low pitch is not marked. A “droop pitch” (Harrington’s term for Tlingit) is shown ... suppression of pitch, as in 4a, not the same as 4a where the drop is gradual. As Hoijer has observed, pitch and stress are not phonemic in Oregon or California Athapaskan (Smith River or Tolowa excepted). Yet they exist on the phonetic level and they deserve to be recorded, particularly because they illuminate problems in reconstruction of protoallophones. (8) Intonation: our small sample gives us falling juncture [...]

new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is given for Galice. The only statement covering Galice says that stress (and pitch) are not phonemic in Oregon/California Athabaskan, attributed to Hoijer; Landar records three phonetic degrees of loudness (primary, secondary, weak) for Harrington's Rogue River Tututni material, while his Galice vocabulary (Hoijer's data) carries no stress marks. Krauss 1979 adds that the PCA languages incl. Galice are toneless and that 'PCA stress systems are still an unresolved problem'; Hoijer 1960 notes the absence of tone phonemes/pitch accent in PCA. Where word stress falls in Galice is therefore undescribed in anything opened.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Landar marks a phonetic secondary (grave) degree in the Tututni transcriptions only; nothing for Galice.
new_statements.exceptions: Smith River/Tolowa excepted from the non-phonemic statement (Bright 1964 posits stress/high pitch in Tolowa).
new_statements.domain_note: Vocabulary items (citation forms) transcribed from Harrington's field notes (Tututni) and Hoijer's Galice data; statement is about phonemic status only, at the level of the whole Oregon/California Athabaskan group, not word-level placement.
new_statements.identity_note: Galice = Galice-Applegate (Taldash, Galice Creek; Applegate/Nabiltse dialect), gali1261, all data from the last speaker Hoxie Simmons (Jacobs 1933-39, Hoijer 1956). Landar 1977's non-phonemic statement covers 'Oregon or California Athapaskan' as a group; his stress-marked transcriptions are Harrington's Rogue River Tututni ('RR', tutu1242), and Sapir 1914's 'stress accent not particularly well marked' is Chasta Costa (also tutu1242), not Galice. Tolowa/Smith River (tolo1259) is explicitly excepted.
